module.wayback_data.checks: Queries the public archive.org index: whether the site is archived, first and last captures, years covered, the closest capture and a few archived URLs.
module.wayback_data.fix:
If a capture or an archived URL shows a secret (password, API key, token, internal address or access): revoke it and replace it before anything else, because a public archive can be read by anyone and may have been copied.
Open the domain's history on web.archive.org and browse the captures from the oldest to the most recent: spot old pages, forms, admin pages, documents and technologies that should no longer be visible.
For each sensitive old URL (admin, backup, `.sql`, `.zip`, `.env`, configuration file, old API, test environment): check whether it still responds on the current site. If it does, delete the file or block access on the server (404 or 403 response) and change any credential it contained.
Ask the Internet Archive to remove the sensitive captures: write to info@archive.org with the exact URLs, the period to exclude and the period during which you controlled the site. No outcome is guaranteed, and a removal does not erase copies made elsewhere.
Compare the date of the first capture with the creation of the domain (WHOIS module): captures of another site, or years without any capture, point to a second-hand domain or a period of parking or expiry. Check that this old content is not tied to you, and redirect useful old URLs to the current pages (301 redirect).
Check: list the archived URLs with the first command in the snippet, then test them with the second one: every removed resource must answer 404 or 403.
Repeat this check after each redesign, migration or change of host, and protect any test or staging environment with authentication: whatever is public can be archived.
module.wayback_data.fix_snippet:
# Wayback CDX
curl -s "https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=example.com&matchType=host&fl=original&collapse=urlkey&limit=100"
# curl
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://example.com/old-backup.zip
module.wayback_data.title: Wayback Machine
module.wayback_data.why: A site's history reveals old pages, old content or old technology that may still be exposed, and the real age of the domain, which helps judge an impersonation or a brand-new site.
wayback_data.unreadable: Unreadable response from the Wayback Machine
